name: Pansy Ho
current_role: Group Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Shun Tak Holdings; co-chairperson, MGM China Holdings
profile: Daughter of the late Macau gaming magnate Stanley Ho, Pansy Ho runs Shun Tak Holdings (property, hotels and the Hong Kong-Macau TurboJET ferries) and holds stakes in MGM China and SJM Holdings. She made more than $1.5bn from MGM China's 2011 IPO and is now a prominent global tourism advocate, serving as a UN Tourism Ambassador.
interesting_fact: She dabbled in Hong Kong show business as an actress in the 1980s and helped promote her sister Josie Ho's acting and singing career.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 she founded the Global Tourism Economy Research Centre, which organises the annual Global Tourism Economy Forum in Macau; she was named a UNWTO Tourism Ambassador in 2018 and became the first official PATA Foundation Ambassador.
notes: Shun Tak has issued a statement warning about false AI-generated content about the group online, so check sources carefully. Her sister Maisy Ho, an executive director, died in April 2026; avoid that topic. Tourism (GTEF, UN Tourism) is the most natural hook. Shun Tak's site blocked scraping, so no email was verified.

name: Maria Del Pino Y Calvo Soleto
current_role: Non-Executive Director of Ferrovial N.V. and President of the Fundación Rafael del Pino
profile: María del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is the eldest child of Ferrovial founder Rafael del Pino y Moreno (d. 2008) and holds about 8.7% of Ferrovial through her company Menosmares, S.L. She has sat on Ferrovial's board since 2006; her brother Rafael is executive chairman. Since 2000 she has also led the family's Fundación Rafael del Pino.
interesting_fact: Her father personally named her president of the Fundación Rafael del Pino when he created it in 2000. Its mission is to train future leaders, and it has since funded hundreds of 'Becas de Excelencia' scholarships for Spanish graduates.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business she interned at the European Commission in Brussels, worked in the International Relations Secretariat of Spain's UCD party from 1979, and later volunteered with the development NGO Codespa until 2000. She studied economics at Universidad Complutense and holds an IESE PDD.
notes: The input spells her name 'Calvo Soleto'; the correct spelling is Calvo-Sotelo. She is very private and has reportedly given only one interview. The best route is through the Fundación Rafael del Pino (general info email), which runs economics and energy-policy events. She also sits on the Princess of Asturias Foundation's board of trustees.

name: Brenninkmeijer family
current_role: Family owners of COFRA Holding AG (Zug, Switzerland), parent of C&A, Bregal Investments and Sunrock; chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, with Florian Brenninkmeyer due to take over in April 2027
profile: This Dutch-German dynasty founded the C&A clothing chain in 1841 and owns it through the Swiss holding company COFRA, alongside private equity (Bregal), real estate and renewable energy investments. Around 2026 the group reported roughly €40bn under management and was handing control to the sixth generation, with Georg Wunderlin as its first non-family CEO.
interesting_fact: C&A takes its name from the initials of the founding brothers Clemens and August Brenninkmeyer, who opened their first textile shop in Sneek, Netherlands, in 1841. Six generations later the business is still entirely family-owned.
deep_cut_fact: Long before ESG became fashionable, Marcel Brenninkmeijer founded Good Energies in 2001 to run COFRA's renewables portfolio. It backed wind and solar developers and the Atlantic Wind Connection offshore transmission backbone, a strong energy hook.
notes: This is a family (hundreds of members), not an individual, and it is famously private. For an energy podcast, the best individual targets are probably COFRA chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, incoming chair Florian Brenninkmeyer, or the Sunrock solar business. Contact is through the COFRA newsroom; no email could be scraped. The family won the 2026 Kellogg Family Leadership Award.

name: Gabriele Volkmann
current_role: Shareholder (heir) in Brose Fahrzeugteile SE & Co. KG, Coburg; no public operating role found
profile: According to Forbes (2018), Gabriele Volkmann is an heir to Brose, the family-owned German auto-parts supplier founded by her great-grandfather Max Brose and built into a global player by her uncle Michael Stoschek. Brose is split between the Stoschek and Volkmann family lines; her mother Christine Volkmann is a shareholder.
interesting_fact: Brose makes mechatronic parts such as window regulators, seat adjusters, door systems and e-bike motors, components that are 'largely invisible to drivers' yet fitted to cars worldwide. It is among the largest family-owned automotive suppliers.
notes: Very private; she appeared on Forbes only in 2018, and almost nothing is published about her personally. German press says the shareholders include Christine Volkmann 'and her eldest daughter', which may be her, but this is unconfirmed. Brose is chaired by Maximilian Stoschek, and he or the Brose press office is the realistic route. Brose's site has no scrapeable press email.
